trigger: any authenticated caller holding a management-group- or service-scope-confined Policy:Read grant calls the pre-existing legacy GET /api/compliance/{policy_id}
summary: Legacy GET /api/compliance/{id} gates its per-agent status fan-out on a bare perm_fn_(Policy,Read) instead of require_fleet_read/authorize_list_read, so a confined caller sees the full unfiltered fleet. Confirmed via git blame this predates #4034 entirely (commits 2fcfb95b50/f20bfd7023, both ancestors of the merge-base). The new /api/v1/compliance/{id} in this diff correctly uses fleet_read_fn_ (require_fleet_read) for the same read. This is the exact sibling-IDOR shape the security preamble's Pattern A calls for, but the PR author already found and filed it pre-governance.
classification: truth (real confinement gap on an unmodified sibling route)
waiver_rationale: Issue #4041 (open, verified via gh issue view) already tracks this exact route + 2 other sibling fan-out gaps (MCP list_agents, guardian per-guard drilldown) as a dedicated migration item. Pre-existing, unchanged by this diff, part of an established incremental Phase-2 migration program (docs/security-reviews/service-scope-phase2-migrations-2026-08.md) with its own ranked backlog. Not this PR's diff to fix.

trigger: any authenticated session (any role, no permission check at all) requests GET /fragments/compliance/summary or GET /fragments/compliance/{id}
summary: The two HTML dashboard fragment routes call only deny_service_scoped_ + auth_fn_ (session exists) with no perm_fn_/RBAC check of any kind, unlike every other route in the file. Not touched by #4034's diff.
waiver_rationale: Issue #4042 (open, verified via gh issue view) already tracks this exact gap, filed by the same author while researching #4034, explicitly out of #4034's own scope.

trigger: a policy trigger row whose config_json column is not valid JSON reaches policy_list_row_json (compliance_model.cpp:48, and the pre-existing compliance_routes.cpp:645/:748)
summary: nlohmann::json::parse(t.config_json, nullptr, false) is never checked for .is_discarded() before being embedded and dumped, unlike the established defensive pattern one function away (policy_store.cpp:213, interval_from_config_json). Empirically verified: dumping a JSON tree containing a discarded node produces the literal non-JSON token <discarded> in the output string (build/test scratch, g++ + the repo's own nlohmann/json.hpp), not an exception and not null. However, repo-wide grep (server/, scripts/) confirms policy_triggers has exactly one writer (PolicyStore::create_policy, policy_store.cpp:677) which always writes config.dump() of a real nlohmann::json object, and no update/migration/seed path writes config_json directly -- so the wrong outcome is proven unreachable given the current writer (E6, caps at LOW).
classification: truth (copied verbatim from the legacy handler this PR was told to byte-match)
waiver_rationale: Not blocking (E6-capped LOW). Deliberately not fixed in this diff: patching only the new compliance_model.cpp call site would make /api/v1/policies emit null for this field while the untouched legacy /api/policies (compliance_routes.cpp:645/:748) still emits the broken <discarded> token for the same row -- a new REST-v1-vs-legacy divergence, which is worse than leaving all three sites consistent. A real fix touches 2 pre-existing call sites outside this diff's scope.

trigger: GET /api/v1/compliance/{id}'s policy-store-degraded 503 (REST), or a store-degraded/gate-denied failure on MCP get_policy_agent_statuses
summary: docs/user-manual/rest-api.md and mcp.md both state this surface is 'Audited: compliance.agent_statuses.view' without qualification, but: (1) the REST route's own store-degraded 503 branch calls no audit_fn_ at all (silent) -- unlike the sibling GET /api/v1/inventory/software, which audits its degraded branch under the domain verb (rest_api_v1.cpp:6888); (2) the MCP get_policy_agent_statuses's store-degraded branch audits via the generic mcp_audit() (action=mcp.get_policy_agent_statuses, target_type=mcp_tool), not the domain verb compliance.agent_statuses.view used on its own success path two lines later. A SIEM/auditor filtering on the documented verb misses every failed/degraded access attempt on both transports.
classification: truth (doc overclaims relative to code; established sibling precedent shows the more complete pattern already exists)
waiver_rationale: No data is disclosed on the unaudited failure paths (503/degraded only); this is an audit-trail completeness gap, not a confidentiality gap. Base MEDIUM (I7), not raised to HIGH -- omission does not conceal a breaking change, security-relevant behaviour, data-loss, migration step, or irreversible operation, only a narrower audit-completeness nuance the codebase already has a documented precedent for tolerating when disclosed (audit-log.md's engine_principal.list/.get REST-only caveat).

trigger: an operator or SIEM author reads docs/user-manual/audit-log.md looking for the compliance.agent_statuses.view verb this PR's own rest-api.md/mcp.md reference
summary: The new audit verb compliance.agent_statuses.view has no entry in the canonical action-verb catalog (docs/user-manual/audit-log.md, 207 rows). Every comparable verb this PR's own reasoning cites as precedent -- guaranteed_state.rule.view (same per-rule fleet-wide fan-out shape, line 228), inventory.software.query (same set-and-proceed posture, line 250), policy.evaluate/policy.remediate (same Policy securable, lines 196-197) -- has a full entry there with target_id/result/SIEM-caveat detail. This one has none.
classification: wording/completeness (the underlying behaviour is documented correctly in rest-api.md/mcp.md; only the centralized catalog is missing the row)
waiver_rationale: Capped at SHOULD/MEDIUM: the behaviour itself is disclosed elsewhere (rest-api.md, mcp.md), so this is a discoverability/completeness gap in one derived catalog, not a concealed behaviour.

trigger: GET /api/v1/compliance/{id} or MCP get_policy_agent_statuses called against a policy whose scope resolves to a very large fleet
summary: PolicyStore::get_policy_agent_statuses (unchanged by this diff -- confirmed empty git diff on policy_store.cpp/.hpp) issues SELECT ... WHERE policy_id = $1 ORDER BY agent_id with no LIMIT clause, unlike query_installed_software/list_policy_fragments which both clamp a limit param. Neither the REST route nor the MCP tool added in this diff accepts or applies a limit. This was already true of the legacy /api/compliance/{id} route; #4034 adds two new consumers (REST v1, MCP) of the same unbounded query.
waiver_rationale: Base MEDIUM (I5 unbounded growth), no raise conditions met (not a reproducible crash, not on a security-serialized path, not a state-machine wedge). The PR's own code comment in mcp_server.cpp already acknowledges the per-agent list 'can grow with fleet size' as a considered tradeoff matching the legacy route's existing shape exactly -- not a regression this PR introduces.
